messages:
carla-pm: Quick sync — we need to lock the network boundary and upgrade choreography for the upcoming VPC/on-prem packaging sprint. want decisions before the PRD cut. :clock1:

liam-eng: Do we have a short list of customer constraints? e.g., no-outbound, only peering, strict egress IPs?

maya-p: From field: three patterns show up repeatedly — 1) managed-peering (customer sets up VPC peering), 2) outbound-allowed-but-restricted (they whitelist our egress IPs), 3) air-gapped/on-prem (no external control plane). Most enterprise customers fall in 1 or 2, a few in 3. :white_check_mark:

aj-engr: Proposal: define three supported network modes in packaging and upgrade tooling:
```
networkMode: managed-peering | egress-whitelist | airgap
```
- managed-peering: prefer direct peering; control plane calls allowed on 443 for telemetry and rollouts.
- egress-whitelist: agent initiates TLS to control plane via known IPs; no inbound allowed.
- airgap: no external comms; use out-of-band bundle exchange (tarball + signed manifest).

liam-eng: Sounds good. For managed-peering we need to document recommended route tables and security group rules. Also decide on fallback behavior — do we auto-fallback to tunnel when peering fails?

carla-pm: Fallback needs product-level decision. auto-fallback reduces downtime but may violate customer policy. We should default to NO auto-fallback and expose opt-in global policy per-customer.

maya-p: Agreed. Field asks: must be explicit opt-in for any tunnel/fallback. Also require audit trail for when fallback used.

aj-engr: Implementation sketch for upgrade choreography (canary -> ramp -> cutover):
1) preflight: validate networkMode, certs, disk space, model artifact checksums
2) canary: upgrade 1 node, verify health checks and evals
3) ramp: 10% -> 50% gradually with metric gates
4) cutover: remaining nodes; rollback on gate failures

Example CLI for operators: 
```
r-inferctl upgrade --bundle v1.2.0 --mode canary --network-mode managed-peering --no-auto-fallback
```

liam-eng: Need concrete gating signals. Proposal:
- infra: kube objects stable for 3 consecutive polls (2m interval)
- serving: 99th p95 token latency regression < +20% vs baseline
- evals: smoke prompt set correctness > 95%
- telemetry: no more than 0.5% error spike in logs

carla-pm: Good. Add human approval gate for any customer in egress-whitelist or airgap.

maya-p: Also add 'migration window' metadata so sales/customer success can schedule low-impact windows.

aj-engr: For airgap upgrades we need signed bundles and an integrity check step:
```
---
bundle: r-infer-bundle-v1.2.0.tar.gz
sha256: 012345...abcd
signed-by: customer-key-2026
instructions: |
  scp bundle -> bastion
  ./r-inferctl apply-bundle --manifest manifest.json
```

deploy-bot: Deploy started for bundle v1.2.0 on staging (deploy-id: d-20260301-007).

liam-eng: Ops concern: how do we surface preflight failures to customers? UX should include a small preflight report and suggested remediation steps (e.g., missing route, expired cert).

carla-pm: Action items: 
- liam-eng: draft recommended network diagrams + SG/route examples (due EOD Fri)
- aj-engr: finalize upgrade CLI flags and gating checks, include telemetry thresholds (due Tue)
- maya-p: create sales playbook text for opt-in fallback + migration windows (due Thu)

maya-p: Also callout compliance: airgap customers need offline attestation steps documented.

carla-pm: Ok lets reconvene next Wed with PRD draft. If anything blocks, ping #product and @carla-pm. :spiral_calendar:

liam-eng: noted. adding small sample policy snippet for opt-in fallback in packaging docs:
```
fallbackPolicy:
  enabled: false
  allowedModes: ["managed-peering"]
  requireApproval: true
```

carla-pm: perfect. thanks everyone. closing thread unless new asks. :thumbsup:
